samples.surface: Narrow exposed yellow/gold PCIe contact-edge surface beside the green PCB.
Exposed contact-edge surface farther along the same sloping lower PCB edge.

connector.evidence: The right image exposes a thin contact-bearing edge on the left boundary of the suspended card, distinct from its broad PCB face and cooler.
connector.uncertainty: The contact surface is narrow and strongly foreshortened, making pixel selection sensitive. These are rough interior surface samples, not mating endpoints. A key notch cannot be resolved reliably.

samples.surface: Solid upper housing/latch surface of the selected PCIe socket beside the CPU area.
Solid side rail of that same socket housing, not its dark opening.

socket.evidence: A portion of the selected long PCIe housing remains visible immediately beside the CPU area. Its rails extend toward the foreground case wall, which hides the lower continuation.
socket.uncertainty: Only a partial housing axis is observable. The internal key and obscured continuation are not localized. Samples are not exact socket endpoints or a gap centerline.

target_identity_assessment.evidence: The historical anchor selects the long socket immediately beside the CPU area, left of the other parallel expansion sockets. The current samples retain that board-relative identity rather than selecting a more visible neighboring socket.
target_identity_assessment.uncertainty: Tracking is based on the motherboard layout and neighboring components. This does not certify that the historical socket choice was correct, or establish clearance or insertion alignment.

next_view.description: An unobstructed close oblique view of the same CPU-adjacent socket and the card contact edge is needed to resolve their keys and the socket portion hidden by the foreground case wall.
